correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all hypotheses and the noise-first factorization. The upper-triangular positivity of any Metzler logarithm follows by a nonnegative exponential series. Resolvent formula of log Q13 is exact; the strictly decreasing integral in d2 crosses zero exactly at the geometric mean via reciprocal substitution, proving the iff threshold for every h>0. Positivity and grid-point mean operator then follow. Finite SciPy checks (132 cases plus six explicit special-case evaluations) corroborate but do not certify the infinite domain.

value.rationale: The source simulation guarantees positivity but may bias expected linear state costs. This theorem provides a complete, step-size-independent correction feasibility test on the minimal directed chain and an exact negative long-range coupling in the forbidden regime, separating mean-correctability from pathwise positivity. The midpoint condition can guide which state-noise distributions allow drift-only calibration; it is not a mere choice of numerical tolerance or isolated finite value.
